channel.title: Ops Journal
channel.description: Field notes on Linux, backups, containers and monitoring, written by an engineer who runs the systems described here. Commands are run before they are written down.

item.title: Too many open files: finding a file descriptor leak before it takes the service down
item.description: EMFILE arrives long before the crash. Reading the per-process limits and counting open descriptors shows which service is leaking and how fast.

item.title: SSH host keys: what that SHA256 fingerprint actually identifies
item.description: The fingerprint prompt is the one moment SSH authentication can be attacked. Knowing what is being compared turns it from a nuisance into a check.

item.title: Crash loops: reading systemd restart policies instead of guessing
item.description: Restart=on-failure and StartLimitBurst decide whether a service recovers or dies. Read them from the running unit, not from the file you think is loaded.

item.title: rsync for backups: the flags that matter and the ones that quietly change what is copied
item.description: A trailing slash changes the entire result, and --delete makes a wrong path destructive. Test with --dry-run until the output matches intent.

item.title: Reading a disk-full incident in the right order
item.description: Space is used, not created. Work from df to du to inodes to open files and the cause is found in minutes instead of an hour.

item.title: Testing whether a remote port is reachable, and what each failure means
item.description: Connection refused, timed out and no route are three different problems. Tell them apart and the fault is localised in one command.

item.title: Finding which process is holding a port, and why kill does not always free it
item.description: Address already in use is a symptom, not a diagnosis. Here is how to find the real owner of a port and why it sometimes refuses to release.

item.title: A health check that does not lie: checking the thing that can actually fail
item.description: A check that returns 200 while the database is unreachable is worse than no check. Here is how to test the dependency, not the process.

item.title: What actually survives a container rebuild: volumes, mounts and the data people lose
item.description: Rebuilding a container is routine until it takes the data with it. Here is which storage survives, which does not, and how to check first.

item.title: A backup you have never restored is not a backup
item.description: Most backup failures are found during a restore, which is the worst possible time. A repeatable restore drill turns that into a non-event.

item.title: systemd timer calendar expressions, and the two that catch everyone
item.description: OnCalendar looks like cron but is not cron. Two expression shapes look correct, parse without error, and run at the wrong time.

item.title: When /var/log eats the disk: finding what actually grew
item.description: A full root filesystem is usually logs, not data. Here is how to find the real culprit in three commands and cap it so it stays capped.
